contentBlocks.text: This week you've explored food chains, webs, and decomposers. Today: see how changing one part affects the whole ecosystem!

Because food webs connect many organisms, a change to just one part can ripple through the whole ecosystem. If foxes disappeared from your Day 2 food web, rabbits would have fewer predators and their population might grow quickly — but then rabbits might eat too much grass, leaving less food for other grass-eaters too. Using your Day 2 food web, explain what might happen if the hawk (or your chosen second predator) suddenly disappeared.
You just traced how one ecosystem change ripples through a whole food web! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Explain how removing one organism from a food web affects other connected organisms
Apply this reasoning to the child's own Day 2 food web
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's food chain, web, and decomposer work.
2. Model the fox-disappearing ripple-effect example.
3. Have the child apply the same reasoning to their own Day 2 food web.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: walk through the effect one step at a time (fewer predators → more prey → less food for prey → ...) rather than requiring the whole chain of reasoning at once
Ready for more: ask the child to think of a real example of this kind of ecosystem ripple effect they may have heard about
This lesson is the week's synthesis moment — connecting individual concepts (chains, webs, decomposers) into one systems-level understanding
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended reasoning activity — check that the child correctly traces a plausible ripple effect (e.g., fewer predators → more of that predator's prey → more pressure on the prey's own food source).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 5 Life Science standard 5-LS2-1, applying this week's ecosystem concepts to a real cause-and-effect scenario within a food web.

generationData.instructions: Explain what might happen to your food web if one predator disappeared.
